newsitem.title: USA: Tiny U.S. transplant patient loses fight for life.
newsitem.headline: Tiny U.S. transplant patient loses fight for life.

text.p: Cheyenne Pyle, who became the world's youngest heart transplant recipient two months ago, has lost her fight for survival after the sudden onset of severe complications, hospital officials said on Friday.
"She died at 2:10 p.m. EST Thursday afternoon," a spokesman for the University of Miami/Jackson Children's Hospital said.

Cheyenne, who was born in November with a severe heart defect, was delivered by caesarean section and received her new heart in her first few hours of life from a stranger whose identity has not been revealed.

Doctors were optimistic immediately after the operation, but Cheyenne had kidney problems and her aorta narrowed as her body struggled to grow and she fought the body's natural tendency to reject the new heart. On Thursday, her major organs apparently gave up.
"Yesterday morning, sometime in the early morning hours, she became gravely ill for reasons not entirely clear to us at this point," the spokesman said.

Her parents were called to the hospital from their home in Fort Lauderdale when it became obvious that Cheyenne's problems were especially serious. She spent her last moments cradled in her parents' arms.
